questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of [Ni(NH₃)₆]Cl₂ is:

solution.explanation: The complex is a cation, so the metal keeps its ordinary name (no -ate ending). NH₃ as a ligand is 'ammine'. Two Cl⁻ counter ions balance the charge, so the complex ion is [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺ and nickel is +2.
steps: Charge of complex ion = +2 (two Cl⁻ outside)
solution.why_others_wrong: '-ate' is used only for anionic complexes; 'ammonia' is not the ligand name for NH₃; the oxidation state of Ni is +2, not +4.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', nomenclature of coordination compounds

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: [CoF₆]³⁻ is a high-spin octahedral complex (atomic number of Co = 27). Its spin-only magnetic moment is about:

solution.explanation: Co³⁺ is 3d⁶. F⁻ is a weak field ligand (Δo < P), so the configuration is t₂g⁴ eg², with four unpaired electrons.
solution.why_others_wrong: 0 BM is the low-spin t₂g⁶ case (as in [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺); 3.87 BM is for three unpaired electrons and 5.92 BM for five.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory: octahedral complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
For the compound K₃[Fe(C₂O₄)₃], match each term in List-I with the corresponding species or value in List-II.

List-I:
A. Central ion
B. Ligand
C. Coordination number
D. Counter ion

List-II:
I. K⁺
II. Fe³⁺
III. C₂O₄²⁻
IV. 6

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Fe³⁺ is the central ion; each oxalate ion, C₂O₄²⁻, is a didentate ligand, so three of them give a coordination number of 6; the three K⁺ ions outside the square brackets are the counter ions.
solution.why_others_wrong: Taking the coordination number as 3 (number of ligands) confuses it with the oxalate entry; K⁺ is outside the coordination sphere and is not the central ion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', definitions of some important terms
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Aqueous solutions containing [Sc(H₂O)₆]³⁺ are colourless.
Reason (R): Sc³⁺ has no d electron, so no d–d transition can take place.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In crystal field theory the colour of a complex comes from excitation of a d electron from a lower to a higher set of d orbitals (d–d transition). Sc³⁺ is 3d⁰, so no such transition is possible and visible light is not absorbed. R explains A.
steps: No d electron → no d–d transition
No absorption in the visible → colourless
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', colour in coordination compounds
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following species are optically active (ox = oxalate, C₂O₄²⁻; en = ethane-1,2-diamine)?
cis-[CrCl₂(ox)₂]³⁻, trans-[CrCl₂(ox)₂]³⁻, [Fe(ox)₃]³⁻, cis-[Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] (square planar), fac-[Co(NH₃)₃Cl₃], cis-[Co(NH₃)₂(en)₂]³⁺

solution.concept: Optical isomerism in octahedral complexes with didentate ligands
solution.explanation: Octahedral complexes with two or three didentate ligands in a cis arrangement have no plane of symmetry and are chiral. A trans arrangement, a square planar complex and the fac isomer of [MA₃B₃] all have a mirror plane.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 misses the tris(oxalato) complex; 4 counts the trans isomer; 5 also counts a planar or fac species, which have mirror planes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', stereoisomerism: optical isomerism

solution.concept: Homoleptic and heteroleptic complexes; cationic and anionic complexes
solution.explanation: A homoleptic complex has only one kind of ligand. [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻ has only CN⁻ ligands and carries a negative charge, so it is homoleptic and anionic.
solution.why_others_wrong: Each of the other complex ions fails one of the two conditions, as shown in the steps.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', definitions of some important terms

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the spectrochemical series, OH⁻ is a weaker field ligand than H₂O.
Statement II: Thiocyanate bonded through sulphur (SCN⁻) produces a larger crystal field splitting than thiocyanate bonded through nitrogen (NCS⁻).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: NCERT's series runs I⁻ < Br⁻ < SCN⁻ < Cl⁻ < S²⁻ < F⁻ < OH⁻ < C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O < NCS⁻ < edta⁴⁻ < NH₃ < en < CN⁻ < CO. OH⁻ comes before H₂O, so it is the weaker field ligand (Statement I true). S-bonded SCN⁻ lies near the weak end and N-bonded NCS⁻ after H₂O, so NCS⁻ gives the larger splitting (Statement II false).
steps: OH⁻ < C₂O₄²⁻ < H₂O → Statement I true
SCN⁻ (weak end) < NCS⁻ → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory: spectrochemical series
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ and [CoF₆]³⁻ are correct (atomic number of Co = 27)?

(a) In both complexes cobalt is in the +3 oxidation state with a 3d⁶ configuration.
(b) [CoF₆]³⁻ is an outer orbital complex in which cobalt uses sp³d² hybrid orbitals.
(c) [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ has four unpaired electrons.
(d) Both complexes are octahedral.
(e) F⁻ is a stronger field ligand than NH₃.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Inner and outer orbital octahedral complexes of Co(III)
solution.explanation: Both are Co³⁺ (3d⁶), six-coordinate and octahedral. NH₃ pairs the 3d electrons, leaving two 3d orbitals free for d²sp³ hybridisation (inner orbital, diamagnetic). F⁻ is weak field, so the 4d orbitals are used (sp³d², outer orbital, four unpaired electrons).
steps: (e) false: F⁻ is a weaker field ligand than NH₃
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', valence bond theory

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the ligand in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I:
A. Ethane-1,2-diamine
B. Oxalate ion
C. Ethylenediaminetetraacetate ion
D. Pyridine

List-II:
I. Anionic, didentate
II. Neutral, unidentate
III. Anionic, hexadentate
IV. Neutral, didentate

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: en, H₂N–CH₂–CH₂–NH₂, is neutral and binds through both N atoms. C₂O₄²⁻ is a dianion that binds through two O atoms. EDTA⁴⁻ binds through two N and four O atoms. Pyridine, C₅H₅N, is neutral and binds only through N.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The crystal field splitting Δo of [CrCl₆]³⁻ is smaller than that of [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺.
Reason (R): Cl⁻ lies before NH₃ in the spectrochemical series, i.e. it is a weaker field ligand.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Dependence of Δo on the ligand
solution.explanation: For the same metal ion in the same oxidation state (Cr³⁺) and the same geometry, Δo depends on the field strength of the ligand. Cl⁻ is a weaker field ligand than NH₃, so the splitting is smaller. R explains A.
steps: Same metal, oxidation state and geometry
Cl⁻ < NH₃ in the spectrochemical series
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field theory
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
According to crystal field theory, in how many of the following octahedral complexes are the eg orbitals completely empty? (Atomic numbers: Ti 22, Cr 24, Mn 25, Fe 26, Co 27, Ni 28; [Mn(CN)₆]³⁻ is low spin.)
[Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, [Cr(H₂O)₆]³⁺, [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺, [CoF₆]³⁻, [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺, [Ni(NH₃)₆]²⁺, [Mn(CN)₆]³⁻

solution.concept: Filling of t₂g and eg orbitals in octahedral complexes
solution.explanation: d¹–d³ ions always have empty eg orbitals. A d⁴–d⁶ ion keeps eg empty only with strong field ligands (low spin). A d⁸ ion must place two electrons in eg whatever the ligand, because t₂g holds only six.
steps: [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺ d⁵ HS: t₂g³ eg² → not empty
[CoF₆]³⁻ d⁶ HS: t₂g⁴ eg² → not empty
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 assumes the strong field NH₃ empties eg in the d⁸ nickel complex; 4 misses the low-spin manganese complex; 3 counts only the d¹ and d³ ions and one d⁶ ion.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Potash alum, K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O, is a double salt, whereas K₃[Al(C₂O₄)₃] is a coordination compound. Assuming complete dissociation of each in dilute aqueous solution, the numbers of ions given by one formula unit of potash alum and of K₃[Al(C₂O₄)₃] are, respectively:

solution.concept: Double salts versus complexes in solution
solution.explanation: A double salt dissociates completely into simple ions in water. A complex ion keeps its identity, so only the counter ions separate from it.
solution.why_others_wrong: '3 and 4' treats alum as a complex ion with two K⁺; '8 and 7' breaks the oxalato complex into Al³⁺ and three C₂O₄²⁻; '4 and 4' uses the half formula KAl(SO₄)₂·12H₂O instead of the formula unit given.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', Werner's theory: double salts and complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the octahedral complex ion in List-I with its d-electron configuration according to crystal field theory in List-II (atomic numbers: Ti 22, Cr 24, Fe 26, Co 27).

List-I:
A. [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺
B. [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺
C. [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺
D. [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺

List-II:
I. t₂g⁶ eg⁰
II. t₂g³ eg²
III. t₂g¹ eg⁰
IV. t₂g³ eg⁰

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Writing t₂g/eg configurations from oxidation state and ligand strength
solution.explanation: Find the d-electron count from the oxidation state, then fill t₂g first; for d⁴–d⁷ use the ligand strength to decide between high and low spin.
steps: Fe³⁺ d⁵ with weak field H₂O → t₂g³ eg² (II)
Co³⁺ d⁶ with NH₃ (Δo > P, diamagnetic) → t₂g⁶ (I)
solution.why_others_wrong: 'A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I' gives Cr³⁺ five d electrons and Fe³⁺ three; 'A-IV, B-III, ...' swaps the d¹ and d³ ions; 'A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II' swaps the Fe³⁺ (d⁵) and Co³⁺ (d⁶) configurations.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', crystal field splitting in octahedral complexes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ and [Ni(CO)₄] are both diamagnetic, although nickel is in different oxidation states in them.
Statement II: [NiCl₄]²⁻ is square planar, because Cl⁻ is a strong field ligand that forces the 3d electrons to pair up.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Four-coordinate nickel complexes in valence bond theory
solution.explanation: In [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ (Ni²⁺, 3d⁸) the strong field CN⁻ pairs the d electrons, giving dsp², square planar and diamagnetic. In [Ni(CO)₄] (Ni⁰) all ten electrons pair in 3d, giving sp³, tetrahedral and diamagnetic. So Statement I is true. Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand: [NiCl₄]²⁻ is sp³, tetrahedral and paramagnetic with two unpaired electrons, so Statement II is false.
steps: [Ni(CO)₄]: Ni(0), sp³, 0 unpaired → Statement I true
[NiCl₄]²⁻: weak field, sp³, tetrahedral, 2 unpaired → Statement II false
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', valence bond theory: tetrahedral and square planar complexes
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Consider the complex K₃[Cr(C₂O₄)₃] (atomic number of Cr = 24). Which of the following statements are correct?

(a) The oxidation state of chromium is +3.
(b) The coordination number of chromium is 6.
(c) The complex ion exists as a pair of enantiomers.
(d) The complex ion has three unpaired electrons.
(e) Its IUPAC name is potassium trioxalatochromium(III).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Oxidation state, coordination number, optical isomerism and magnetism of a tris(chelate) complex
solution.explanation: x + 3(−2) = −3 gives Cr(III), 3d³. Three didentate oxalate ions give coordination number 6. Like [Co(en)₃]³⁺, a tris(didentate) octahedral ion is chiral. A d³ ion has t₂g³, three unpaired electrons. As the complex is an anion, the metal name ends in -ate: potassium trioxalatochromate(III).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Coordination Compounds', nomenclature and isomerism

questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: The sodium fusion extract of an organic compound is acidified with acetic acid and lead acetate solution is added. A black precipitate forms. This shows the presence of:

solution.concept: Test for sulphur in Lassaigne's extract
solution.explanation: During sodium fusion, sulphur of the compound is converted into sodium sulphide. With lead acetate, sulphide ions give black lead sulphide: S²⁻ + Pb²⁺ → PbS (black).
solution.why_others_wrong: Nitrogen is shown by Prussian blue, chlorine by a white AgCl precipitate, and phosphorus by the yellow ammonium molybdate test.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', qualitative analysis: test for sulphur

questions.question_text: An organic compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.67% hydrogen and 53.33% oxygen by mass. Its empirical formula is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: Divide each percentage by the atomic mass and then by the smallest quotient.
solution.why_others_wrong: CHO ignores the factor 2 for hydrogen; C₂H₄O doubles C and H but not O; CH₃O misreads the hydrogen ratio.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: An organic compound containing only C, H and O has 54.55% carbon and 9.09% hydrogen by mass. 0.88 g of its vapour occupies 224 mL at STP. Its molecular formula is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16; molar volume at STP = 22400 mL):

solution.concept: Molecular formula from percentage composition and molar mass
solution.explanation: Molar mass = mass / moles of vapour. Oxygen is found by difference. Then each element's share of the molar mass gives the number of atoms.
solution.why_others_wrong: C₂H₄O is only the empirical formula (M = 44); C₃H₄O₃ and C₅H₁₂O have M = 88 but the wrong percentages of C and H.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis

questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Nitrogen, sulphur and halogens present in an organic compound cannot be detected directly with the usual reagents for their ions, so the compound is first fused with sodium.
Reason (R): These elements are covalently bonded in organic compounds; fusion with sodium converts them into ionic compounds such as NaCN, Na₂S and NaX.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Ionic tests (Prussian blue, nitroprusside, AgNO₃) need the elements as ions. Because they are covalently bonded in the compound, fusion with sodium is used to convert them into ionic salts, which are extracted with water. R explains A.
steps: Elements covalently bonded → no ions to test
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', qualitative analysis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the test for nitrogen, the sodium fusion extract is boiled with iron(II) sulphate and then acidified with concentrated sulphuric acid; on heating, some iron(II) ions are oxidised to iron(III) ions, which react with the hexacyanidoferrate(II) formed.
Statement II: The Prussian blue precipitate obtained in this test is iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II), Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃·xH₂O.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Chemistry of the Prussian blue test
solution.explanation: NaCN in the extract gives Na₄[Fe(CN)₆] with iron(II) sulphate. On heating with concentrated H₂SO₄, some Fe²⁺ is oxidised to Fe³⁺, which with [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻ gives Prussian blue, Fe₄[Fe(CN)₆]₃·xH₂O. Both statements are true.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', test for nitrogen
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text: In a Dumas determination, 0.30 g of an organic compound gave 56 mL of nitrogen gas, corrected to STP. If another 0.30 g of the same compound were analysed by Kjeldahl's method (assume the method is applicable), the ammonia evolved would exactly neutralise what volume of 0.10 M H₂SO₄? (Molar volume at STP = 22400 mL)

solution.concept: Linking the Dumas and Kjeldahl methods through the moles of nitrogen atoms
solution.explanation: Each N₂ molecule carries two N atoms, and each N atom gives one NH₃ in Kjeldahl's method. Two NH₃ neutralise one H₂SO₄.
solution.why_others_wrong: 50 mL treats H₂SO₄ as monobasic; 12.5 mL takes one N atom per N₂ molecule; 250 mL divides 0.0025 mol by 0.010 M instead of 0.10 M (a slip of one decimal place).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', estimation of nitrogen

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the quantitative analysis of organic compounds are correct?

(a) In the Carius method, the halogen of the compound is finally weighed as a silver halide.
(b) Kjeldahl's method is suitable for estimating nitrogen in azo compounds.
(c) In the estimation of sulphur, the sulphuric acid formed is precipitated as barium sulphate.
(d) In the estimation of carbon and hydrogen, the carbon dioxide formed is absorbed in concentrated potassium hydroxide solution.
(e) The percentage of oxygen is usually found by direct weighing of the oxygen set free from the compound.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Halogen is weighed as AgX (Carius) and sulphur as BaSO₄. CO₂ is absorbed in KOH and water in anhydrous CaCl₂. Kjeldahl's method fails for nitro and azo compounds and for nitrogen in a ring (e.g. pyridine), because their nitrogen is not converted into ammonium sulphate. Oxygen is usually estimated by difference.
steps: (b) false: azo nitrogen is not converted to (NH₄)₂SO₄
(e) false: %O = 100 − sum of the other percentages
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', quantitative analysis

questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH₂–CH(Br)–CH₂–OH is:

solution.concept: Numbering a chain that carries a principal functional group and a substituent
solution.explanation: –OH is the principal functional group (suffix -ol) and must get the lowest locant, so the carbon carrying –OH is C-1. Bromine is then on C-2. Halogens are always cited as prefixes.
solution.why_others_wrong: '3-Bromobutan-4-ol' and '2-Bromobutan-4-ol' number from the wrong end; '1-Hydroxy-2-bromobutane' cites the principal group as a prefix.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of compounds having functional groups

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following groups, attached to a carbon chain, show an electron-releasing (+I) inductive effect?
–CH₃, –CH₂CH₃, –C(CH₃)₃, –NO₂, –CN, –COOH, –Cl, –COOR

solution.explanation: Alkyl groups such as methyl and ethyl release electrons (+I). Nitro, cyano, carboxyl, ester and halogen groups withdraw electrons (−I).
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 or 5 wrongly add the ester or carboxyl group, whose carbonyl carbon withdraws electrons; 2 leaves out one of the alkyl groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', inductive effect

Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ethyne, HC≡CH, is a linear molecule.
Reason (R): Each carbon atom of ethyne is sp hybridised, and its two sp hybrid orbitals point in opposite directions at 180°.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Each carbon uses its two sp orbitals to form σ bonds to H and to the other carbon. As the two sp orbitals are at 180°, H–C–C–H lies on a straight line. R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', shapes of carbon compounds
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ethyl ethanoate (CH₃COOC₂H₅) and methyl propanoate (C₂H₅COOCH₃) are metamers.
Statement II: Pentan-2-ol and pentan-3-ol are chain isomers.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Metamers have the same functional group with different alkyl groups on either side of it; both esters are C₄H₈O₂ with the alkyl groups distributed differently about –COO–, so Statement I is true. Pentan-2-ol and pentan-3-ol have the same chain and differ only in the position of –OH: they are position isomers, so Statement II is false.
steps: Esters: same group, different alkyl groups on either side → metamers
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural isomerism
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the species in List-I with its description in List-II.

List-I:
A. (CH₃)₃C⁺
B. CH₃•
C. CH₃⁻
D. NH₃

List-II:
I. Has a carbon atom with six valence electrons and a vacant p orbital
II. Has a carbon atom with an unpaired electron
III. Has a carbon atom carrying an unshared pair, with pyramidal shape
IV. A neutral molecule that acts as a nucleophile

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Carbocations, free radicals, carbanions and nucleophiles
solution.explanation: A carbocation has a sextet on the sp² carbon with an empty p orbital; a free radical has an odd (unpaired) electron; a carbanion has an unshared pair on an sp³ carbon and is pyramidal; NH₃ is a neutral molecule with a lone pair, so it acts as a nucleophile.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the carbocation and free radical, the radical and carbanion, or treat NH₃ as the carbocation.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', fission of a covalent bond
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the representation of organic molecules are correct?

(a) In a bond-line formula, carbon and hydrogen atoms are not shown and the lines represent carbon–carbon bonds drawn in a zig-zag fashion.
(b) In a bond-line formula, the terminals of the lines represent methyl groups unless a functional group is indicated there.
(c) The condensed formula CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ represents hexane.
(d) In a wedge-and-dash formula, a dashed wedge represents a bond projecting away from the observer.
(e) In a bond-line formula, heteroatoms such as oxygen and nitrogen are not shown.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In bond-line formulas only the heteroatoms and the hydrogens attached to them are written; C and H are implied, and line ends are methyl groups. CH₃(CH₂)₃CH₃ has five carbons (pentane). A dashed wedge points away from the observer, a solid wedge towards the observer.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', structural representations

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following molecules contain at least one sp-hybridised carbon atom?
CO₂, HCN, CH₂=C=CH₂, CH₃CN, CH₂=CH₂, C₆H₆, CH₃–C≡CH, CH₃CHO

solution.explanation: A carbon with two σ bonds and two π bonds (a triple bond, or two double bonds) is sp hybridised.
steps: Ethene, benzene, ethanal: only sp² and sp³
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 usually misses the central carbon of allene or the CO₂ carbon; 6 counts the carbonyl carbon of ethanal, which is sp²; 3 counts only the C≡C and C≡N compounds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hybridisation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: How many structural isomers are possible for trichlorobenzene, C₆H₃Cl₃ (all three chlorine atoms on the benzene ring)?

solution.explanation: Place three identical substituents on the six ring positions and remove arrangements that are the same after rotating or turning over the ring.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 forgets the unsymmetrical 1,2,4-isomer; 4 counts 1,2,4- and 1,2,5- (the same compound) separately; 6 counts numbering variants as different compounds.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(OH)–CH₂–CH=CH₂ is:

solution.concept: Lowest locant to the principal functional group (–OH) in preference to a double bond
solution.explanation: The parent chain has six carbons and contains both the C=C and the C bearing –OH. The suffix group –OH gets the lowest locant: numbering from the left gives –OH at C-3 (from the right it would be C-4). The double bond is then C5=C6 and the methyl group is on C-2.
steps: From the left: OH at 3; from the right: OH at 4 → number from the left
solution.why_others_wrong: Names with '-1-en' give the double bond the lowest locant, which is wrong when –OH is the principal group; '2-methylhex-5-en-4-ol' mixes the two numberings.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Carbanions behave as nucleophiles.
Reason (R): The negatively charged carbon of a carbanion carries an unshared pair of electrons that it can donate to an electron-deficient centre.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: A nucleophile is an electron-pair donor that seeks an electron-deficient centre. The carbanion carbon has an unshared electron pair, so it acts as a nucleophile. R explains A.
steps: Carbanion: carbon with an unshared pair and negative charge
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nucleophiles and carbanions
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The conversion of ethanol into ethene by heating with concentrated sulphuric acid is an elimination reaction.
Statement II: In a rearrangement reaction, atoms or groups shift within the same molecule to give a structural isomer of it.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Loss of H₂O from adjacent carbon atoms of ethanol to form a C=C bond is an elimination. A rearrangement reaction changes the skeleton or positions of groups within one molecule (e.g. n-hexane → 2-methylpentane), giving an isomer. Both statements are true.
steps: Rearrangement: groups shift within the molecule → isomer
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', types of organic reactions
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the compound in List-I with its IUPAC name in List-II.

List-I:
A. CH₃–CH=CH–CHO
B. CH₃–CO–CH=CH₂
C. HC≡C–CH₂–OH
D. CH₃–CH(CN)–CH₃

List-II:
I. Prop-2-yn-1-ol
II. 2-Methylpropanenitrile
III. But-2-enal
IV. But-3-en-2-one

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Names of unsaturated and polyfunctional compounds
solution.explanation: In each name the principal group (–CHO, C=O, –OH, –CN) gets the lowest locant; the carbon of –CHO and of –CN is counted as C-1 of the chain.
steps: CH₃CH=CHCHO: C-1 is CHO, C=C at 2 → but-2-enal (III)
CH₃COCH=CH₂: C=O at 2, C=C at 3 → but-3-en-2-one (IV)
HC≡CCH₂OH: OH at 1, C≡C at 2 → prop-2-yn-1-ol (I)
(CH₃)₂CHCN: CN carbon is C-1, methyl at 2 → 2-methylpropanenitrile (II)
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap the aldehyde and the ketone, or the alcohol and the nitrile.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about electronic effects are correct?

(a) In chloroethane, CH₃–CH₂–Cl, the carbon atom bonded to chlorine carries a partial positive charge.
(b) In chloroethane, the carbon atom farther from chlorine carries a smaller partial positive charge than the carbon bonded to chlorine.
(c) The inductive effect is transmitted only through π bonds.
(d) The electromeric effect is a permanent effect.
(e) Alkyl groups such as –CH₃ show an electron-releasing inductive (+I) effect.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Cl pulls the C–Cl bond electrons, making C-1 δ+; C-1 in turn pulls a little from C-2, which becomes δδ+, so the effect weakens along the chain of σ bonds. The electromeric effect is temporary, operating only when an attacking reagent is present. Alkyl groups are +I.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', electron movement in organic reactions

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which of the following is the strongest acid?

solution.explanation: The −I effect of chlorine stabilises the carboxylate ion and increases acidity, but the effect fades rapidly as the number of bonds between Cl and –COO⁻ increases. It is greatest when Cl is on the α-carbon.
steps: Cl on β (C-3) or γ (C-4): weaker
solution.why_others_wrong: Moving chlorine to C-3 or C-4 weakens its effect on the carboxyl group; butanoic acid has no electron-withdrawing group.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', inductive effect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among all the structural isomers of the monochloroalkane C₅H₁₁Cl, how many contain a chiral carbon atom (a carbon bonded to four different groups)?

solution.concept: Generating structural isomers and finding chiral centres
solution.explanation: C₅H₁₁Cl has eight structural isomers (three on the pentane chain, four on the 2-methylbutane chain, one on the 2,2-dimethylpropane chain). Check each carbon bearing Cl or a branch.
steps: 2-Methylbutane: 1-Cl (C-2: H, CH₃, C₂H₅, CH₂Cl → yes), 2-Cl (two CH₃ → no), 3-Cl i.e. 2-chloro-3-methylbutane (yes), 4-Cl i.e. 1-chloro-3-methylbutane (no)
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 misses 1-chloro-2-methylbutane, whose chiral carbon does not carry chlorine; 4 or 5 wrongly count 3-chloropentane or 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, which have two identical groups.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text: The IUPAC name of CH₃–CH(C₂H₅)–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃ is:

solution.concept: Longest chain and lowest locants at the first point of difference
solution.explanation: The longest chain runs from the CH₃ of the ethyl group to the far CH₃: eight carbons (octane), with methyl groups on three carbons. Numbering from the right gives {3, 4, 6}; from the left {3, 5, 6}. At the first point of difference 4 < 5, so number from the right.
steps: Longest chain = 8 C (through the ethyl group)
solution.why_others_wrong: Names ending in 'heptane' miss the longer chain that runs through the ethyl group (an ethyl group at C-2 or C-6 always means a longer chain exists); 3,5,6- numbers from the wrong end.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', nomenclature of branched alkanes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An sp-hybridised carbon atom attracts bonding electrons more strongly than an sp³-hybridised carbon atom.
Reason (R): The greater the s character of a hybrid orbital, the farther its electrons lie from the nucleus.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: s character and electronegativity of carbon
solution.explanation: s orbitals are held closer to the nucleus than p orbitals, so a hybrid orbital with more s character (sp: 50%) keeps its electrons nearer the nucleus. An sp carbon is therefore more electronegative than sp² or sp³ carbon. A is true; R reverses the relationship and is false.
steps: More s character → electrons closer to the nucleus
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', hybridisation and electronegativity
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For chloroethene, CH₂=CH–Cl, a canonical structure with a positive charge on chlorine and a negative charge on the terminal CH₂ carbon contributes to the resonance hybrid.
Statement II: As a result, the carbon–chlorine bond in chloroethene acquires partial double bond character.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Resonance (+R) involving a halogen lone pair
solution.explanation: A lone pair of chlorine is delocalised into the C=C π bond, giving ⁻CH₂–CH=Cl⁺ as a minor canonical structure. Because a C=Cl double bond appears in one contributor, the real C–Cl bond has partial double bond character. Both statements are true.
steps: Hybrid: C–Cl with partial double bond character
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance effect
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the observation in List-I with the electronic effect mainly responsible for it in List-II.

List-I:
A. Stabilisation of propene by delocalisation of the σ electrons of its methyl C–H bonds into the π bond
B. Equal length of the two carbon–oxygen bonds in the methanoate ion, HCOO⁻
C. Chloroethanoic acid is a stronger acid than ethanoic acid
D. Complete shift of the π electrons of an alkene to one carbon when H⁺ approaches

List-II:
I. Inductive effect
II. Electromeric effect
III. Hyperconjugation
IV. Resonance effect

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Choosing the electronic effect that explains an observation
solution.explanation: σ–π delocalisation of C–H bonds is hyperconjugation; equal C–O bonds arise because the negative charge is delocalised over both oxygens (resonance); Cl withdraws electrons through σ bonds (−I), stabilising ClCH₂COO⁻; the temporary, complete shift of a π pair on the approach of a reagent is the electromeric effect.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes confuse resonance with hyperconjugation, or the permanent inductive effect with the temporary electromeric effect.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', electronic displacements
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following pairs are resonance (canonical) structures of the same species, rather than different compounds?

(a) CH₃–CO–CH₃ and CH₂=C(OH)–CH₃
(b) The two Kekulé structures of benzene
(c) CH₂=CH–CH₂⁺ and ⁺CH₂–CH=CH₂
(d) CH₃–O–N=O and CH₃–NO₂
(e) The two structures of the ethanoate ion with the negative charge on either oxygen atom

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Canonical structures differ only in the positions of electrons; the positions of all nuclei stay the same. In (a) a hydrogen atom has moved (the two are different compounds), and in (d) the atoms are connected differently (methyl nitrite and nitromethane are isomers). In (b), (c) and (e) only π electrons or charges move.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques', resonance structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Methane burns completely according to CH₄(g) + 2O₂(g) → CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l); ΔcH = −890 kJ mol⁻¹. The heat released by the complete combustion of 4.0 g of methane is (C = 12, H = 1):

solution.explanation: The enthalpy change is for one mole of methane, so scale it by the number of moles burnt.
solution.why_others_wrong: 890 kJ is for one whole mole; 55.6 kJ is the heat per gram (890/16); 3560 kJ multiplies by 4 instead of dividing by the molar mass.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: combustion

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: In the sulphonation of benzene with fuming sulphuric acid (oleum), the electrophile that attacks the ring is:

solution.explanation: Fuming sulphuric acid contains dissolved SO₃. Sulphur in SO₃ is strongly electron-deficient, so SO₃ is the electrophile that attacks the π electrons of the ring, giving benzenesulphonic acid.
solution.why_others_wrong: H₃O⁺ does not substitute the ring; HSO₄⁻ and SO₄²⁻ are anions (electron-rich) and cannot act as electrophiles.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', electrophilic substitution reactions: sulphonation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the method of preparing an alkene in List-I with the name of the process in List-II.

List-I:
A. Heating an alkyl halide with alcoholic KOH
B. Heating a vicinal dihalide with zinc metal
C. Heating an alcohol with concentrated H₂SO₄
D. Hydrogenating an alkyne over Lindlar's catalyst

List-II:
I. Partial reduction
II. Acidic dehydration
III. Dehydrohalogenation
IV. Dehalogenation

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Alcoholic KOH removes HX (dehydrohalogenation); zinc removes two halogen atoms from adjacent carbons (dehalogenation); concentrated H₂SO₄ removes water from an alcohol (acidic dehydration); Lindlar's catalyst stops hydrogenation of an alkyne at the alkene (partial reduction).
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes interchange the halogen-removing processes or the dehydration and partial reduction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkenes
solution.final_answer: Option C: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Among isomeric alkanes, the straight-chain isomer has the highest boiling point.
Statement II: 2,2-Dimethylpropane (neopentane) has a higher boiling point than 2-methylbutane (isopentane).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Effect of branching on boiling points of alkanes
solution.explanation: Branching makes a molecule more compact (nearly spherical), reducing its surface area and therefore the van der Waals forces. So the boiling point falls as branching increases: n-pentane (309 K) > isopentane (301 K) > neopentane (282.5 K). Statement I is true and Statement II false.
steps: More branching → smaller surface area → weaker van der Waals forces → lower b.p.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: physical properties
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 1,2-Dibromopropane, CH₃–CHBr–CH₂Br, is converted into propyne by treatment with alcoholic KOH followed by sodamide. The mass of propyne obtained from 20.2 g of 1,2-dibromopropane, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80):

solution.concept: Preparation of alkynes from vicinal dihalides
solution.explanation: Two molecules of HBr are removed from one molecule of the vicinal dihalide, so 1 mol of dihalide gives 1 mol of propyne.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.2 g is the mass of propene (only one HBr removed); 8.0 g and 2.0 g double or halve the mole ratio.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkynes from vicinal dihalides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Methane is chlorinated in light until it is converted completely into tetrachloromethane:
CH₄ + 4Cl₂ → CCl₄ + 4HCl
The minimum mass of chlorine needed for 1.6 g of methane is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5):

solution.explanation: Each substitution replaces one H by Cl and uses one Cl₂ molecule (the other Cl atom leaves as HCl). Four hydrogens are replaced, so 4 mol Cl₂ per mol CH₄.
solution.why_others_wrong: 7.1 g uses one Cl₂ per CH₄; 14.2 g uses Cl (35.5) instead of Cl₂ (71) for 0.40 mol; 56.8 g counts eight Cl₂ per CH₄.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: halogenation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
How many of the following alkenes give propanone as one of the products of ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O)?
2-Methylpropene, 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, 2-methylbut-2-ene, but-2-ene, propene, 2-methylbut-1-ene, 3-methylbut-1-ene

solution.concept: Ozonolysis: each doubly bonded carbon becomes a carbonyl carbon
solution.explanation: Propanone, (CH₃)₂C=O, is formed only from a doubly bonded carbon that carries two methyl groups, i.e. an alkene containing (CH₃)₂C=.
steps: But-2-ene → ethanal only; propene → ethanal + methanal
solution.why_others_wrong: 4 or 5 count 2-methylbut-1-ene or 3-methylbut-1-ene, whose (CH₃) groups are not both on a doubly bonded carbon; 2 misses one of the three correct alkenes.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: ozonolysis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a single alkyl halide is used in the Wurtz reaction, the alkane formed has twice the number of carbon atoms present in the alkyl halide.
Reason (R): In the Wurtz reaction, two alkyl groups from two molecules of the alkyl halide are joined by a new C–C bond when the halide is treated with sodium in dry ether.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: 2R–X + 2Na → R–R + 2NaX. Because the product joins two identical R groups, it has double the carbon atoms of R–X (e.g. CH₃Br → ethane, C₂H₅Br → butane). R is why A is true.
steps: Carbon count of R–R = 2 × carbon count of R
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkanes: Wurtz reaction
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about benzene are correct?

(a) Under ordinary conditions benzene prefers electrophilic substitution to addition.
(b) All six carbon atoms of benzene are sp² hybridised and the ring is planar.
(c) Benzene has (4n + 2) π electrons with n = 1.
(d) Benzene is hydrogenated over nickel at high temperature and pressure mainly to cyclohexene.
(e) The Kekulé structure with fixed alternate single and double bonds explains the equal lengths of all the C–C bonds.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Substitution keeps the aromatic sextet, so benzene favours it. The six sp² carbons form a planar ring whose six π electrons (n = 1 in 4n + 2) are delocalised. Hydrogenation over Ni goes on to cyclohexane. A Kekulé structure would have unequal bonds; the equal 139 pm bonds are explained by resonance.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', aromatic hydrocarbons: structure of benzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Equal masses (7.8 g each) of benzene, C₆H₆, and ethyne, C₂H₂, are burnt completely in oxygen. The ratio of the volumes of carbon dioxide formed from benzene and from ethyne, measured under the same conditions, is (C = 12, H = 1):

solution.concept: Same empirical formula → same CO₂ per gram
solution.explanation: Benzene and ethyne both have the empirical formula CH. Equal masses therefore contain the same number of moles of carbon atoms, and each carbon atom gives one CO₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: 3 : 1 compares the carbon atoms per molecule (6 : 2) without using moles; 1 : 3 compares the moles of the two hydrocarbons; 6 : 1 compares the carbon atoms per molecule with one mole of ethyne giving one CO₂.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', combustion of hydrocarbons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The addition of HBr to propene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide takes place by a free-radical mechanism.
Statement II: Addition of HBr to an unsymmetrical alkene in the presence of a peroxide is also called the peroxide effect or Kharash effect.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Benzoyl peroxide forms free radicals that generate Br• from HBr; Br• adds to give the more stable free radical, so the product is 1-bromopropane (anti-Markovnikov). NCERT calls this the peroxide or Kharash effect. Both statements are true.
steps: Br• adds to CH₂ end → secondary radical → 1-bromopropane
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: anti-Markovnikov addition
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Each of the three xylenes (o-, m- and p-dimethylbenzene) is mononitrated on the ring. Counting only structurally different products, the total number of mononitro derivatives that can be obtained from all three xylenes together is:

solution.concept: Counting distinct ring positions in disubstituted benzenes
solution.explanation: Use the symmetry of each xylene to find how many ring positions are different.
steps: p-Xylene (1,4): all four free positions equivalent → 1 product
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 misses position 2 of m-xylene (between the methyl groups); 7 counts positions 4 and 6 of m-xylene separately; 4 assumes each xylene has the same number of products as toluene's o/p.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', isomerism in aromatic compounds and electrophilic substitution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: An alkene X, C₆H₁₂, on ozonolysis (O₃, then Zn/H₂O) gives one mole of ethanal and one mole of butanone per mole of X. X is:

solution.explanation: Join the two carbonyl carbons by a double bond after removing the oxygen atoms: CH₃CH=O + O=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ → CH₃CH=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃. The longest chain containing the double bond has five carbons, with a methyl group on C-3.
solution.why_others_wrong: Hex-2-ene gives ethanal and butanal; 2-methylpent-2-ene gives propanone and propanal; 3-methylpent-1-ene gives methanal and 2-methylbutanal.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkenes: ozonolysis

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Hydrogenation of but-2-yne over palladium on charcoal partially deactivated with quinoline gives cis-but-2-ene.
Reason (R): Reduction of but-2-yne with sodium in liquid ammonia gives trans-but-2-ene.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Partial reduction of alkynes to cis and trans alkenes
solution.explanation: Lindlar's catalyst stops the hydrogenation at the alkene stage and gives the cis alkene. Sodium in liquid ammonia gives the trans alkene. Both statements are true, but R describes a different reagent and a different product; it does not explain why Lindlar reduction gives the cis isomer.
steps: R is about another reaction → not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', preparation of alkenes from alkynes
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the alkane in List-I with the number of structurally different monochloro derivatives it can give on free-radical chlorination (List-II).

List-I:
A. 2,2-Dimethylpropane
B. n-Butane
C. n-Pentane
D. 3-Methylpentane

List-II:
I. 2
II. 4
III. 1
IV. 3

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Counting different kinds of hydrogen atoms
solution.explanation: Each set of equivalent hydrogen atoms gives one monochloro product.
steps: 3-Methylpentane: C1, C2, C3 and the branch CH₃ → 4 (II)
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes miscount n-pentane (forgetting C-3) or 3-methylpentane (forgetting the branch methyl or the tertiary C-3).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: halogenation
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the chemical reactions of alkanes are correct?

(a) On pyrolysis, dodecane gives a mixture containing heptane and pentene, among other products.
(b) Under normal conditions alkanes are generally inert towards acids, bases and most oxidising and reducing agents.
(c) Free-radical chlorination of methane proceeds through a carbocation intermediate.
(d) Heating n-alkanes with anhydrous AlCl₃ and HCl gas converts them into branched-chain isomers.
(e) Complete combustion of an alkane gives carbon monoxide and hydrogen.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Pyrolysis (cracking) breaks large alkanes into smaller alkanes and alkenes, e.g. C₁₂H₂₆ → C₇H₁₆ + C₅H₁₀ + other products. Alkanes are generally inert to most reagents under ordinary conditions. Halogenation is a free-radical chain reaction. Anhydrous AlCl₃/HCl isomerises n-alkanes. Complete combustion gives CO₂ and H₂O.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Chemistry, 'Hydrocarbons', alkanes: chemical properties

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Primary and secondary alcohols are converted into alkyl chlorides by heating with concentrated hydrochloric acid in the presence of:

solution.explanation: Anhydrous zinc chloride is used with concentrated HCl to replace the –OH group of primary and secondary alcohols by –Cl; tertiary alcohols react with concentrated HCl simply by shaking at room temperature.
solution.why_others_wrong: Red phosphorus is used with bromine or iodine (to give PBr₃/PI₃ in situ); aqueous NaOH would hydrolyse an alkyl halide back to the alcohol; dry ether is the solvent for Grignard and Wurtz reactions.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation of haloalkanes from alcohols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Chlorobenzene is treated with chloromethane and sodium in dry ether (Wurtz–Fittig reaction):
C₆H₅Cl + CH₃Cl + 2Na → C₆H₅CH₃ + 2NaCl
The mass of toluene formed from 11.25 g of chlorobenzene, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, H = 1, Cl = 35.5):

solution.explanation: One mole of chlorobenzene gives one mole of toluene.
solution.why_others_wrong: 7.7 g is the biphenyl that the Fittig reaction (two aryl halides) would give; 18.4 g and 4.6 g double or halve the 1 : 1 ratio.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', reactions of haloarenes with metals

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Free-radical halogenation of alkanes is not a good method for preparing a particular haloalkane, because it gives a mixture of isomeric mono- and polyhaloalkanes.
Statement II: Ethene reacts with hydrogen chloride to give chloroethane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Chlorination of an alkane such as butane gives several monochloro isomers and polychloro products that are hard to separate, so the method is unsuitable for a pure product (Statement I true). Hydrogen halides add to alkenes: CH₂=CH₂ + HCl → CH₃CH₂Cl (Statement II true).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', preparation of haloalkanes
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about optical activity are correct?

(a) A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation.
(b) The two enantiomers of a compound rotate plane-polarised light by equal amounts but in opposite directions.
(c) Butan-2-ol is a chiral molecule.
(d) A laevorotatory compound is indicated by the sign (+) before its name.
(e) Propan-2-ol is a chiral molecule.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In a racemic mixture the rotation due to one enantiomer is cancelled by the other. Butan-2-ol has a carbon bonded to H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅, so it is chiral; propan-2-ol's C-2 carries two CH₃ groups. Laevorotatory compounds carry the sign (−); dextrorotatory ones (+).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', optical isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Freon-12 is made from tetrachloromethane by the Swarts reaction:
3CCl₄ + 2SbF₃ → 3CCl₂F₂ + 2SbCl₃
The mass of CCl₂F₂ obtained from 15.4 g of CCl₄, assuming complete conversion, is (C = 12, Cl = 35.5, F = 19):

solution.explanation: CCl₄ and CCl₂F₂ are in the mole ratio 3 : 3, i.e. 1 : 1.
solution.why_others_wrong: 13.8 g is for CCl₃F (one F only); 10.5 g is for CClF₃ (three F); 8.1 g wrongly uses the 2 : 3 ratio of SbF₃ to CCl₂F₂ for CCl₄.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds: freons

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An SN2 reaction at a chiral carbon atom gives a product with the inverted configuration.
Reason (R): In an SN2 reaction the nucleophile attacks the carbon atom from the side opposite to the leaving group.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Because the nucleophile approaches from the back, the other three groups are pushed over to the other side as the leaving group departs, like an umbrella turning inside out. This backside attack is why the configuration is inverted. R explains A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN2 mechanism and stereochemistry
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction of haloalkanes in List-I with its feature in List-II.

List-I:
A. SN2 reaction
B. SN1 reaction
C. β-Elimination (dehydrohalogenation)
D. Reaction with magnesium in dry ether

List-II:
I. Carbocation intermediate; racemisation of a chiral substrate
II. Organometallic product with a polar carbon–magnesium bond
III. Alkene formed by loss of HX from adjacent carbon atoms
IV. Single step with inversion of configuration

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: SN2 is concerted with inversion; SN1 goes through a planar carbocation and racemises a chiral substrate; β-elimination removes H from the β-carbon and X from the α-carbon to give an alkene; Mg in dry ether gives the Grignard reagent R–MgX.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other codes swap SN1 and SN2, or the elimination and Grignard entries.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', chemical reactions of haloalkanes
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Iodoform was used earlier as an antiseptic, but because of its objectionable smell it has been replaced by other formulations containing iodine.
Statement II: Freons are extremely stable, unreactive, non-toxic, non-corrosive and easily liquefiable gases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Both statements follow NCERT's account: iodoform's antiseptic action comes from free iodine, but its smell led to its replacement; freons (chlorofluorocarbons) are stable, non-toxic, non-corrosive, easily liquefied gases, which is why they were used in refrigeration and aerosol propellants.
steps: Iodoform: antiseptic, replaced due to smell → true
Freons: stable, unreactive, easily liquefied → true
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', polyhalogen compounds
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, (CH₃)₃C–Br, are correct?

(a) It is a secondary alkyl halide.
(b) Its hydrolysis in water takes place mainly by the SN1 mechanism.
(c) The rate of its SN1 hydrolysis does not depend on the concentration of the nucleophile.
(d) When heated with alcoholic KOH it gives 2-methylpropene.
(e) Its hydrolysis by SN2 gives a product with inverted configuration at a chiral carbon.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Behaviour of a tertiary alkyl halide
solution.explanation: The C–Br carbon is bonded to three carbons, so the halide is tertiary. Tertiary halides react by SN1, whose rate depends only on [RX]. With alcoholic KOH they undergo β-elimination to (CH₃)₂C=CH₂. The molecule has no chiral carbon (three identical CH₃ groups) and is too hindered for SN2.
steps: (e) false: no chiral carbon; SN2 is hindered
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN1 mechanism and elimination

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The hydrolysis of 2-bromo-2-methylpropane in a large excess of water follows the SN1 mechanism, with rate = k[(CH₃)₃CBr] and k = 6.93 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹ at a certain temperature. The time taken for 75% of the alkyl bromide to react is (ln 2 = 0.693):

solution.concept: First-order kinetics of an SN1 reaction
solution.explanation: An SN1 reaction is first order in the alkyl halide, so its half-life is constant: t½ = 0.693/k. 75% reaction means 25% left, i.e. two half-lives.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1000 s is one half-life (50% reaction); 4000 s is four half-lives; 500 s halves t½.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN1 mechanism (first-order rate)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 7.85 g of bromobenzene is converted completely into phenylmagnesium bromide in dry ether. The Grignard reagent is treated with dry ice (solid CO₂) and the product is hydrolysed with dilute acid. Assuming every step is complete, the mass of the organic acid obtained is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Br = 80):

solution.explanation: C₆H₅Br → C₆H₅MgBr → (CO₂) C₆H₅COOMgBr → (H₃O⁺) C₆H₅COOH. One mole of bromobenzene gives one mole of benzoic acid.
solution.why_others_wrong: 12.2 g takes 0.10 mol; 3.9 g is the benzene formed if the Grignard reagent were hydrolysed by water before reacting with CO₂; 6.8 g is the mass of phenylethanoic acid (M = 136), which would need one more carbon atom than CO₂ supplies.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', Grignard reagents; 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Propene is treated with HBr in the presence of benzoyl peroxide to give X. X is heated with ethanolic KCN to give Y, and Y is reduced with lithium aluminium hydride to give Z. Z is:

solution.concept: Anti-Markovnikov addition, nucleophilic substitution by CN⁻ and reduction of nitriles
solution.explanation: With peroxide, HBr adds anti-Markovnikov: X = CH₃CH₂CH₂Br. KCN gives the nitrile Y = CH₃CH₂CH₂CN (one carbon added). LiAlH₄ reduces –C≡N to –CH₂NH₂: Z = CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂NH₂.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2-Methylpropan-1-amine would come from 2-bromopropane (no peroxide); propan-1-amine forgets the carbon added by cyanide; N-propylmethanamine would come from an isocyanide, which forms with AgCN, not KCN.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', nucleophilic substitution; 'Amines', reduction of nitriles

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Tertiary alkyl halides undergo SN1 reactions faster than primary alkyl halides.
Reason (R): An SN1 reaction takes place in a single step without forming any intermediate.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: SN1 takes place in two steps: slow ionisation of R–X to a carbocation, then fast attack of the nucleophile. The more stable the carbocation (3° > 2° > 1°), the faster the reaction, so A is true. R describes an SN2 reaction and is false.
steps: R false: SN1 has a carbocation intermediate
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Haloalkanes and Haloarenes', SN1 mechanism
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4.2 g of propene is treated with diborane and the product is oxidised with alkaline hydrogen peroxide (hydroboration–oxidation). Assuming complete conversion, the alcohol formed and its mass are (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16):

solution.explanation: In hydroboration–oxidation, water is effectively added so that –OH ends up on the less substituted carbon: propene gives propan-1-ol. One mole of propene gives one mole of alcohol.
solution.why_others_wrong: Propan-2-ol is the product of acid-catalysed hydration (Markovnikov); 3.0 g halves the mole ratio; 4.2 g simply repeats the mass of propene and ignores the added H₂O.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of alcohols: hydroboration–oxidation

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 4.4 g of ethanal is reduced completely to ethanol by catalytic hydrogenation over nickel. The volume of hydrogen consumed, measured at STP, is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16; molar volume at STP = 22.4 L mol⁻¹):

solution.concept: Reduction of aldehydes to primary alcohols
solution.explanation: CH₃CHO + H₂ → CH₃CH₂OH: one mole of H₂ per mole of aldehyde.
solution.why_others_wrong: 4.48 L assumes two moles of H₂ per mole of ethanal; 1.12 L halves the ratio; 22.4 L is for one whole mole.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of alcohols by reduction of aldehydes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Methanoic acid (formic acid) gets its common name from the source from which it was first obtained. This source is:

solution.explanation: Methanoic acid was first obtained from red ants; its common name comes from the Latin formica, meaning ant.
solution.why_others_wrong: Vinegar gives acetic acid (acetum); rancid butter gives butyric acid (butyrum); goat fat gives caproic acid.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', nomenclature of carboxylic acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Ethanol has a much higher boiling point than its isomer methoxymethane.
Reason (R): Ethanol molecules are associated through intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which are absent in methoxymethane.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Hydrogen bonding and boiling points of alcohols and ethers
solution.explanation: Both have M = 46 g mol⁻¹, but ethanol has an O–H group and forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds; an ether has no hydrogen on oxygen. Extra energy is needed to break the hydrogen bonds, so ethanol boils much higher. R explains A.
steps: Ether: no O–H → only dipole interactions
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', physical properties of ethers
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A primary alcohol can be oxidised to an aldehyde by CrO₃ in an anhydrous medium.
Statement II: Tertiary alcohols are readily oxidised to ketones by CrO₃.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Using CrO₃ in an anhydrous medium (or PCC) stops the oxidation of a primary alcohol at the aldehyde stage (Statement I true). Tertiary alcohols have no hydrogen on the carbinol carbon and are not oxidised to carbonyl compounds by such reagents (Statement II false).
steps: R₃C–OH: no H on the C–OH carbon → no ketone
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', chemical reactions of alcohols: oxidation
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following methods can be used to prepare phenol?

(a) Heating chlorobenzene with NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, followed by acidification
(b) Fusing sodium benzenesulphonate with NaOH, followed by acidification
(c) Warming an aqueous solution of benzenediazonium chloride
(d) Air oxidation of cumene to cumene hydroperoxide, followed by treatment with dilute acid
(e) Heating benzene with dilute aqueous NaOH

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Phenol is obtained from haloarenes, from benzenesulphonic acid, from diazonium salts and from cumene. Benzene itself does not react with aqueous NaOH.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', preparation of phenols

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: A mixture of ethanoic acid and propanoic acid is heated with a mixture of methanol and ethanol in the presence of a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid. How many different esters can be formed?

solution.concept: Esterification: each acid can combine with each alcohol
solution.explanation: An ester R–COO–R′ takes its acyl part from the acid and its alkyl part from the alcohol. Two acids × two alcohols give four combinations.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 pairs each acid with only one alcohol; 3 treats ethyl ethanoate and methyl propanoate (which are isomers) as the same compound; 6 counts acid–acid or alcohol–alcohol products as esters.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', esterification

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 5.8 g of propanone reacts completely with semicarbazide, H₂N–CO–NH–NH₂, in weakly acidic solution to form propanone semicarbazone. The mass of the semicarbazone formed is (C = 12, H = 1, N = 14, O = 16):

solution.concept: Reaction of carbonyl compounds with ammonia derivatives
solution.explanation: >C=O + H₂N–Z → >C=N–Z + H₂O. Propanone gives (CH₃)₂C=N–NH–CO–NH₂, C₄H₉N₃O (M = 115).
solution.why_others_wrong: 13.3 g forgets that water is eliminated; 7.2 g is for the hydrazone (C₃H₈N₂); 5.8 g just repeats the mass of propanone.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', reactions with ammonia derivatives

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: 7.025 g of benzoyl chloride is hydrogenated over palladium on barium sulphate (Rosenmund reduction). Assuming complete conversion, the mass of benzaldehyde formed is (C = 12, H = 1, O = 16, Cl = 35.5):

solution.explanation: C₆H₅COCl + H₂ → C₆H₅CHO + HCl. The poisoned catalyst stops the reduction at the aldehyde.
solution.why_others_wrong: 5.4 g is benzyl alcohol (over-reduction, which the Pd–BaSO₄ catalyst prevents); 6.1 g is benzoic acid (hydrolysis); 10.6 g takes 0.10 mol.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', preparation of aldehydes from acyl chlorides

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Ethyl methyl ether (methoxyethane), CH₃–O–CH₂CH₃, is heated with one equivalent of concentrated HI. The main products are:

solution.concept: Cleavage of unsymmetrical ethers by HI
solution.explanation: The ether oxygen is first protonated. The iodide ion then attacks by SN2, choosing the less hindered (smaller) alkyl group, so iodomethane and ethanol are formed.
steps: I⁻ attacks the less hindered CH₃ (SN2)
solution.why_others_wrong: CH₃CH₂I + CH₃OH would need I⁻ to attack the more hindered ethyl group; the other two options are not balanced products of a single cleavage.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', reactions of ethers: cleavage of the C–O bond

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Methanal undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated alkali.
Reason (R): Methanal is a gas at room temperature.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The Cannizzaro reaction is shown by aldehydes that have no α-hydrogen; methanal has none, so it disproportionates into methanol and methanoate. R is a true physical property of methanal, but it has nothing to do with the reaction.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids', Cannizzaro reaction; physical properties
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Alcohols can act both as Brönsted acids and as Brönsted bases.
Statement II: Sodium ethoxide is a stronger base than sodium hydroxide.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.concept: Acidic and basic character of alcohols
solution.explanation: An alcohol donates the O–H proton (acid) and its oxygen lone pairs accept a proton (base). Alcohols are weaker acids than water, so the alkoxide ion is a better proton acceptor than hydroxide: sodium ethoxide is a stronger base than NaOH. Both statements are true.
steps: ROH weaker acid than H₂O → RO⁻ stronger base than OH⁻
solution.ncert_reference: Class 12 Chemistry, 'Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers', acidity of alcohols
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Match the reaction in List-I with its name in List-II.

List-I:
A. An alkyl halide is heated with a sodium alkoxide
B. An aldehyde having α-hydrogen is treated with dilute NaOH
C. An aldehyde having no α-hydrogen is heated with concentrated NaOH
D. A carboxylic acid having α-hydrogen is treated with Cl₂ and a little red phosphorus

List-II:
I. Cannizzaro reaction
II. Hell–Volhard–Zelinsky reaction
III. Williamson synthesis
IV. Aldol reaction

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Alkoxide + alkyl halide → ether (Williamson); α-H aldehyde + dilute alkali → β-hydroxy aldehyde (aldol); no α-H aldehyde + concentrated alkali → alcohol + carboxylate (Cannizzaro); α-halogenation of acids with X₂/red P → HVZ reaction.
